newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures erase gains to end mostly lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures erase gains to end mostly lower.

text.p: U.S. debt futures finished mostly lower, erasing the day's gains in light volume following the Treasury's five-year note auction, traders said.
"Despite the price action, we've pretty much held in here," one floor source said.

September T-bonds fell to 108-20/32 in reaction to the auction, which produced an average yield of 6.568 percent, versus estimates of 6.55 percent. The bid-to-cover ratio was 2.13 and noncompetitive bids were at $534 million.
The 108-20/32 level was Monday's low and also represents the 3-1/2-week settlement low.
However, September T-bonds did not linger at the day's lows, and settled above the 100-day moving average at 108-23/32, while Eurodollars also ended above their day's lows.

Most Eurodollars settled unchanged, even though selling was more aggressive in the Eurodollar pit and the calender spreads widened out. For instance, the September to September 1997 spread widened more than 0.80, from about 0.40, one trader said.
"But again, we are not seeing a lot of volume," he said, adding that total estimated volume was 250,000.

Likewise, estimated bond futures volume was around 280,000, with most of the volume attributed to traders rolling positions in September into December. While the September contract does not expire until September 19, December becomes the lead contract month at the start of Friday's pit session.
One large U.S. firm sold 3,000 September bonds at the opening, and then bought 2,000 September later in the day.

Traders were mixed on whether or not buying would once again in the Tokyo and London markets. Some attributed the strong foreign bid merely to the dollar/yen rally, while others said foreign central bank buying would continue.
Some traders said nervousness ahead of Thursday's weekly U.S. jobless claims report and the revised second-quarter real Gross Domestic Product report could contain overnight losses.
Claims are expected to rise to 330,000, versus 327,000 in the previous week, while real GDP is seen up 4.2 percent.

At the end of pit trade, September bonds were off 05/32 at 108-25/32, 10-year notes were off 02/32 at 107-07/32, munibonds were up 10/32 114-27/32, December Eurodollars were unchanged at 94.08, March Eurodollars were also steady at 93.91 and March T-bills were also flat at 94.50.
